threads.body:
The new maintenance-bot routing depends on `facts["is_maintenance_bot"]`, but single-PR refresh runs (`--pr-number`) reuse cached `stored_result` entries for all other PRs and those cached entries never get re-classified/re-routed (only `route`+`facts` are stored, not thread classifications). That means existing open Renovate/otelbot PRs can remain on the old routing/approval policy until they happen to be rebuilt in a full run, which undermines the intent of this change.

Consider adding an explicit cache/schema invalidation step (e.g., bump dashboard-state version and force a full rebuild when an older cache is loaded) so the new maintenance-bot behavior applies immediately across all open PRs.

 def route_pr(facts: dict[str, Any], classifications: list[dict[str, Any]]) -> str:
     counts = action_counts(classifications)
-    # otelbot PRs have no human author, so an author-owed thread points at
-    # nobody who can act; skip that check for them. They also reach merge-ready
-    # on a single approval (these are low-risk dependency-bump PRs).
-    is_otelbot = facts.get("is_otelbot_author")
+    # Copilot PRs are mapped back to a human author when possible. Maintenance
+    # bot PRs have no useful author route and need only one approval.
+    is_maintenance_bot = facts.get("is_maintenance_bot")
+    required_approvals = 1 if is_maintenance_bot else 2

threads.body: `detect_human_delegator()` now only filters out the `copilot` committer slug, so it can incorrectly treat other bot committers (e.g., `app/...` or `... [bot]`) as the “human delegator” and set the effective author to a bot login. This can break the intended routing (author buckets pointing at a non-human).

threads.body:
`STATE_VERSION` is used for both `dashboard-state.json` and `notification-state.json` via the shared `load_state_file()` helper. With the new strict version check, bumping `STATE_VERSION` will also discard the existing Slack notification cadence state, which can lead to a wave of “initial” notifications once the next valid notification state is written/read.

If the goal is only to invalidate cached PR routing, consider versioning the dashboard cache separately (or exempting `notification-state.json` from this version gate / adding a migration path).

replies.body: No code change needed. The notification-state reset is intentional here: we chose the simpler shared state-version bump so the first post-merge run starts from fresh state instead of adding separate dashboard/notification migration paths.

threads.body: `first_human_committer_login` only checks `commits[0]`, so it can miss a human delegator when the first commit is authored/committed by Copilot (or another bot) but a later commit has a human committer. This also makes the implementation inconsistent with the function name (it doesn’t actually find the *first* human committer in the list).

Fixed in https://github.com/open-telemetry/semantic-conventions-genai/commit/c2bbfe5324640d375d8af5d278a45351f239ca49.

Kept the first-commit-only heuristic intentionally, because the first commit is the Copilot PR initiation signal and later commits should not silently change the dashboard effective author. The misleading `first_human_committer_login` name was replaced with `human_author_for_copilot_pr`, and the helper now only rejects empty or known Copilot committer logins.
